transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-15
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samira Khatri (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connell (Redwood), Maya Patel (Helix Head of ML), Tom Brunner (Helix CTO), Aisha Khan (Helix Security), Ravi Singh (Helix Platform)

[00:00] Samira (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. quick intro, i'm samira, i'll run the demo and diego and liam are on for the deeper infra and benchmark bits.
[00:12] Maya (Helix): thanks samira, quick context — we're evaluating options for an LLM layer to power triage and note-summarization across our EHR attachments. main concerns: latency at P95 under 350ms for short prompts, cost per 1k tokens, and of course PHI handling / VPC options.
[00:30] Samira: perfect, that's exactly what we'll focus on — model catalog selection, how the console surfaces benchmarks and compatibility matrices, and how redwood optimize recommends quant and batching to hit cost/latency tradeoffs.
[00:45] Diego (Redwood SE): just quick qual — are you currently running any models in prod? what's the stack?
[00:52] Tom (Helix): we have an internal stack using huggingface-instances and some in-house caching right now. latency is ok for async tasks but not for near-real-time triage. we also have strict network rules; ideally we'd prefer a private deployment in our VPC or dedicated capacity with peering.
[01:10] Diego: understood. redwood supports hosted, dedicated reserved pools, and private deploys into a customer VPC. dedicated is often the sweet spot for predictable throughput and isolation — Private for full control/air-gapped. both support KMS integration and audit logs.
[01:30] Aisha (Helix Security): quick security question — SOC2 and encryption at rest, and do you support HSM/KMS key rotation? we also need SSO/SAML with SCIM for role provisioning.
[01:42] Samira: yes, we have SOC2 Type II, KMS for key management and HSM options for private deployments. SAML/SSO with SCIM for provisioning is supported; i'll follow up with the security package.
[01:55] Liam (Redwood): i'll jump into the catalog — starting console view.
[02:00] [Screen share starts - Console - Model Catalog]
[02:12] Liam: here is the model catalog — we surface curated open models (llama-2 variants, mistral, redwood-verified checkpoints) with performance profiles. the compatibility matrix shows runtime support (quantized fp8, int8), kernel preferences, and hardware notes per model.
[02:30] Maya: can you show an example of the compatibility matrix? we need to know if a model's kv cache layout will break our long-form notes flow.
[02:38] Liam: sure — here's the matrix row for llama-2-70b: shows kv-cache layout standard, recommended quant profile: int8-ggml-ish (we call it int8-compat), and notes about kernel selection on a40 vs h100. small transcription note: sometimes the matrix says 'K V cache' in the UI exports but it's the standard KV cache.
[02:58] Diego: for triage with short contexts (200-500 tokens) we often recommend a smaller model family — 13b or 7b — unless you need complex reasoning. the console has end-to-end measured benchmarks: latency P50/P95 on common instance shapes, tokens/sec for streaming, and a cost-estimator that uses your expected token counts.
[03:20] Tom: what's the delta for inference quality between a 13b quantized model and a full fp16 70b in your benchmarks?
[03:28] Diego: it depends on the task — for summarization and triage we've seen 13b fine-tuned or instruction-tuned models give near-equal ROUGE/F1 in many workloads with much lower latency and cost. the console also surfaces model-specific evals per prompt set — you can upload your prompts to get a quick scoring.
[03:46] Maya: how accurate are the console benchmark numbers compared to a customer's real-world dataset? we worry about synthetic bias.
[03:52] Liam: good point — benchmarks are run on representative workloads and we provide a benchmark harness (script) for customers to run the same tests in their env or on dedicated capacity. the results usually align within +/-10% for latency; quality varies with dataset but the per-prompt eval helps. we'll share the script.
[04:12] Samira: i'll flag a next step to share the harness and a sample prompt set you can run in your environment or in our POC.
[04:20] [05:00] Aisha: about data residency and retention — we need logs for audit but only minimal token retention for debugging. how configurable is retention and do you have per-customer log segregation?
[04:35] Diego: retention is configurable per deployment. hosted keeps short-term traces by default; dedicated and private give you full control. audit logs and token-level cost breakdowns are available; for sensitive workloads we recommend private with KMS and restricted log retention.
[04:50] Ravi (Helix Platform): on integration — how does model pinning and rollouts work? we need canary traffic to a new model then automatic fallback if latency or quality regressions occur.
[05:02] Liam: rollouts are built into the console — you can create a route that pins a model version, set a canary percent, define SLO thresholds (latency/cost/quality), and automatic fallback policies. for example, if P95 latency > 500ms drop back to a cheaper model variant.
[05:20] Maya: tell me about Optimize — how does it pick quant profiles? we have some tasks where quantization kills quality.
[05:27] Diego: Optimize combines observed token-length distributions, your SLOs, and model-specific sensitivity profiles. it recommends quant bitwidths, batching sizes, and cache TTLs. there's also a quality regression detector: tie a prompt set to an eval and it alerts if generation metrics degrade. for sensitive prompts we can exclude them from auto-quant recommendations.
[05:50] Tom: curious about kernel and compilation — if we run in our VPC on A100s, will the runtime auto-select kernels?
[05:58] Liam: yes, the serving runtime does kernel selection based on architecture and sequence-length distributions. note: some model builds (we call them optimized builds) are tuned for H100 vs A100 and the compatibility matrix indicates the recommended build. occasionally naming in the exports is a bit off (we've seen 'h one hundred' transcribed) but the matrix has the right flags.
[06:18] [06:40] Maya: can you demo uploading our small prompt set and show the eval UI?
[06:45] [Screen share - Console -> Evals]
[06:50] Liam: upload csv, select model candidates (we'll pick llama-2-13b-int8, mistral-7b-fp16, redwood-alpha-13b-int8), run batch eval. here's an example run — redwood shows per-prompt scores, token counts, latency distribution, and a side-by-side quality delta table.
[07:12] Diego: note that the 'redwood-alpha-13b' is a placeholder in this demo; in prod you'll see the specific open checkpoints. sometimes the exporter transcription says 'redwood alpha' which confuses customers.
[07:28] Maya: what's the best way to balance cost vs latency for our 350ms P95 goal?
[07:35] Diego: common approach: pick a model in the 7b-13b family, enable int8 quant (if quality tolerates), use prefix caching for repeated contexts, set batch size of 1-4 for low latency, and reserve dedicated capacity sized for your peak concurrency. Optimize can auto-tune batch sizes for min latency under your throughput.
[07:56] Aisha: do you support per-route RBAC? our clinicians shouldn't have access to raw patient prompt logs.
[08:02] Samira: yes RBAC is per-route and integrates with SAML/SCIM. logs can be redacted and retention limited by role.
[08:12] Tom: cost estimation — can you show an example cost calc for 1M tokens/month across a dedicated 13b int8 pool?
[08:20] [Screen share - Cost Estimator]
[08:25] Liam: here's a back of napkin: with int8 13b on dedicated pool, our estimator shows about $X per 1M tokens (demo uses placeholder). i'll send exact pricing for committed tiers.
[08:38] Maya: we'd like to run a POC. ideally a week-long run on dedicated capacity, running our benchmark harness and measuring P95, throughput, cost. we'd also want to test private/pod peering if needed.
[08:50] Samira: totally doable. POC plan: provision a dedicated pool for 1 week, we run your prompts, measure metrics, and iterate on quant/batch configs. next steps will include security onboarding so you can push data into the harness securely.
[09:02] Aisha: for onboarding, we'll need a data processing agreement and details on where logs are stored.
[09:08] Samira: i'll include the DPA and security pack in the follow-up.
[09:12] [09:20] Diego: quick technical nuance — if you plan to use long histories, be mindful of KV cache growth and model state size. some of the open models have different KV cache strategies which affect memory footprint; the compatibility matrix flags models with non-standard KV layout.
[09:34] Maya: that's helpful — can you include recommended memory footprints for each model build in the matrix?
[09:40] Liam: yes we can export a CSV with memory, recommended GPU type, quant profiles, and known caveats.
[09:46] Tom: any mention of competitors in this space — how do you compare to hosted APIs like OpenAI for latency/cost?
[09:54] Samira: high level: hosted large-vendor APIs are easy but expensive and less flexible for private deployments. Redwood focuses on predictable economics across dedicated/private, with tooling to tune quant/batching and run benchs. we'll share benchmarking comparisons in the follow-up (note: public comparisons vary by workload).
[10:10] Maya: ok final asks for follow-up: 1) pricing and committed capacity options, 2) security pack (SOC2, KMS, SSO/SCIM, DPA), 3) benchmark harness + sample prompt upload instructions, 4) model compatibility matrix CSV, 5) schedule POC start window next week.
[10:30] Samira: we'll get that over. action items as discussed.
[10:40] Liam: any final technical questions?
[10:44] Ravi: just one — can we route traffic by region and fall back to a cheaper region if capacity constrained?
[10:49] Diego: yes, smart routing supports region/cost/latency policies and automatic fallback to model variants or alternate regions.
[10:58] Maya: great — appreciate the demo, this was very useful. we'll confirm POC dataset and timeline offline.
[11:06] Samira: thanks everyone. recap: Samira to send pricing & security docs, diego to share benchmark harness and runbook, liam to export compatibility matrix CSV and example evals. Maya to confirm dataset and SLA.
[11:26] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings: 'int8-compat' sometimes shown as 'in t eight compat', 'KV cache' as 'K V cache', model names can be split. speaker overlaps and filler words retained to keep authenticity.
